1: Late night in LA: a man suddenly drops onto the roof of a cab that is waiting for a fare.
2: That night, the passenger in an ordinary cabbie's car was a hired killer.
3: At LA airport, a man in a gray suit and sunglasses swaps bags with a stranger and disappears. He would be Max's fare tonight.
4: At the cab company garage, Max polishes his taxi clean again today and tucks a photo of an island into the driver's seat.
5: Max has driven a cab in LA for twelve years. In front of the driver's seat is a photo of a tropical island, a reminder of the limousine company he dreams of starting someday.
6: Max's cab rolls down the sunset-lit streets of LA. Tonight begins like any other day.
7: His first fare that night is Annie, a federal prosecutor. Max bets her on the route, and he wins.
8: Annie tells Max she played a string instrument in high school, opening up to a driver she has just met.
9: Max talks about the limo company he'll start someday: a car so nice you won't want to get out even after you reach the airport.
10: Judging only by Annie's clothes and bag, Max guesses that she's a lawyer.
11: Annie is nervous about tomorrow's first trial, so Max shows her his own secret getaway: a photo of an island in the Maldives.
12: As she gets out, Annie hands Max her business card. But Max just stands there holding it, hesitating.
13: Then comes the next fare: a man in a gray suit, Vincent.
14: Vincent says he hates LA and tells a story about a man who died on the subway. Nobody noticed for six hours, he says.
15: Vincent asks how many years Max has been a driver, and Max answers twelve, though it's only temporary work.
16: Vincent says he has five stops to make tonight and offers Max $600 to drive him until dawn.
17: Max waits behind the building. Then a man falls from an upstairs window onto his cab.
18: Vincent loads the body into the trunk and tells the terrified Max to keep driving.
19: The cab pulls out again with a corpse in the trunk. Max can think only of a way out of this nightmare.
20: Meanwhile, Fanning, a narcotics detective, arrives at the apartment where the body fell. The dead man was his informant.
21: Inside the cab, Vincent says calmly, as if it were nothing, that one man dying isn't such a big deal.
22: Police pull the cab over because of the broken windshield. Just as they order the trunk opened, a radio call about a shooting comes in, and the cops simply leave.
23: Vincent keeps Max tied to the steering wheel and goes up into a building to deal with his second target, a lawyer.
24: Meanwhile, Max shouts for help to two men passing through the alley. But they rob Max's wallet and Vincent's bag, and Vincent's gun cuts them down.
25: Leaving the robbers Vincent shot behind, the cab goes back to racing through the night streets.
26: At the same time, Detective Fanning hears testimony that a taxi was at the scene, and he suspects the cabbie is involved.
27: Vincent takes Max into a jazz club. He sits down across from the club's owner, Daniel.
28: Max realizes that Daniel is Vincent's target and gives him an anxious look.
29: Daniel tells the story of the night he played with Miles Davis. But Daniel's face freezes at what Vincent says next: he is the third target.
30: Vincent says he'll spare Daniel if he answers a question about Miles Davis, but in the end he pulls the trigger.
31: If Max doesn't go to the hospital, his mother will call the cab company. So Vincent takes Max all the way to her hospital room.
32: In the hospital elevator they pass Detective Fanning, but neither recognizes the other.
33: His mother scolds Max for bringing flowers, but warmly reaches out her hand to Vincent.
34: His mother brags that her son started a limousine company. It was a lie Max had made up for her.
35: The moment he leaves the room, Max snatches Vincent's bag and runs down the stairs.
36: Then Max seizes Vincent's bag and escapes, and from an overpass he throws away the laptop holding the list of targets.
37: Meanwhile, at the morgue, gunshot wounds from the same killer keep turning up. Fanning realizes this is a serial contract killing.
38: When Max brings up his mother as they drive, Vincent tells him a story about his own father.
39: Vincent asks Max, who has been in a temporary job for twelve years, why he still hasn't started.
40: Having lost his list, Vincent tells Max to pose as him and get a new list from Felix, the drug cartel boss who is the client.
41: Fanning goes to FBI agent Pedrosa and tells him about the murders that happened tonight.
42: Max sits in front of Felix pretending to be Vincent. He's terrified, but he coolly fires back just as Vincent would.
43: When Vincent says he lost the list, Felix tells him a Mexican fairy tale about a creature that carries off bad children.
44: Felix hands over the information on the last two targets, and Max gets out of the club safely.
45: But Felix orders his men to take care of Vincent. Meanwhile, the FBI begins chasing the case too.
46: The FBI is on its way to catch Vincent, but Fanning can't shake the feeling that the cabbie isn't the real killer.
47: A helicopter takes off, and the FBI assault team heads to Club Fever.
48: Vincent tells Max to call Annie. He says to be sure to do it if he survives.
49: Vincent stares silently out the window. The cab heads to Club Fever.
50: Club Fever, where the fourth target is. The FBI, Felix's men, and Vincent all converge at once.
51: Gunfire erupts and the crowd descends into chaos. Detective Fanning pulls out Max, who has been mistaken for Vincent, but Fanning is soon shot down by Vincent.
52: Vincent puts Max back in the cab. He tells him to drive downtown for the remaining target, and mocks Max for letting his life slip away while he only dreams.
53: Back in the cab, Max shouts back at Vincent for the first time. He says Vincent isn't a human being.
54: Those words make Max decide to stop Vincent, and he floors the accelerator. Then he flips the cab over.
55: Max crawls out of the overturned cab and sees the last target's photo on Vincent's laptop. It's Annie, the prosecutor who was his first fare that night.
56: Police approach the wrecked cab, and Max is arrested.
57: Max shakes off the police and runs to the federal building. He calls Annie and tells her Vincent is on his way.
58: Annie doesn't believe Max's call, but in the meantime Vincent has already reached her office floor.
59: Max sneaks into the federal building and gets hold of a guard's gun.
60: In the dark office, Vincent stalks Annie. Then Max appears holding the guard's gun.
61: Annie crawls across the dark office floor to evade Vincent.
62: Max shoots Vincent and gets Annie out. The two take the elevator down and run to the subway station.
63: Vincent keeps coming even after being shot. Max and Annie flee into the subway.
64: Covered in blood, Vincent searches the subway cars one by one for the two of them.
65: In the stopped subway train, Max and Vincent face each other with a single door between them and fire at the same moment. Vincent is the one who goes down.
66: Vincent dies sitting in a subway seat, and Max and Annie walk out of the station into the dawn.
67: That was Collateral, directed by Michael Mann. It drew attention as Tom Cruise's first turn as a cold-blooded villain.
68: The story of a dreaming cabbie who took the wheel in a single night. Could you have stood up to Vincent the way Max did? Let us know in the comments.
